title: Fiber colimits lift a prescribed base cone through a cocartesian fibration
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, simplicial pullbacks and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations and fibers of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and right join cones and relative colimit diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $J$ be any small simplicial set and let $p:E\to B$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories, all in one fixed sufficiently large universe. For an edge $e:b\to b\prime$, a transport functor $e_!:E_b\to E_{b\prime}$ is equipped with a simplicial map $H:E_b\times\Delta^1\to E$ over $e\circ\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^1}$, restricting to the fiber inclusion at $0$ and to the fiber inclusion composed with $e_!$ at $1$, with $p$-cocartesian edges on every $\{v\}\times\Delta^1$. Say that $e_!$ preserves $J$-indexed colimits if, for every $J$-diagram and every colimit cocone in $E_b$, its image under $e_!$ is a colimit cocone in $E_{b\prime}$. Suppose every fiber $E_b$ admits colimits of all $J$-indexed diagrams and every edge transport preserves these colimits. Given simplicial maps $h:J\to E$ and $g:J^{\triangleright}\to B$ with $ph=g|_J$ exactly, there exists a $p$-colimit diagram $v:J^{\triangleright}\to E$ with $v|_J=h$ and $pv=g$ exactly. The base cone $g$ is arbitrary and need not be a colimit in $B$. Neither $J$ nor the fibers are assumed filtered or weakly contractible. If $J=\varnothing$, the hypotheses require initial objects in all fibers and their preservation.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.1.11, printed pp. 266-267, including its prescribed-base lifting square; proof uses Proposition 4.3.1.10 and pointwise cocartesian transport. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical cone-lifting theorem.

proof.text: Let $s=g(*)$ be the image of the cone vertex and let $\eta:J\times\Delta^1\to B$ be the coherent transformation from $g|_J$ to the constant diagram at $s$, obtained by restricting $g$ along the map that is the identity at time $0$ and collapses $J\times\{1\}$ to the cone vertex. Since $p$ is an inner fibration with horn-cocartesian lifts of every edge out of every vertex, [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] shows that these lifts are cocartesian in the mapping-space sense, so $p$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]; conversely every edge that node calls cocartesian is $p$-cocartesian in the horn sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $p$, $K=J$, $A=h$, $G=\Delta_Js$, and this $\eta$. It supplies a diagram $h':J\to E_s$ and a simplicial map $Q_0:J\times\Delta^1\to E$ over $\eta$, with $Q_0|_{J\times\{0\}}=h$, $Q_0|_{J\times\{1\}}=h'$, and every time edge $Q_0|_{\{j\}\times\Delta^1}$ $p$-cocartesian. The restriction really is in the strict fiber because $p h'=\Delta_Js$.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.1.11 proof, pp. 266-267: form the map $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$ and choose its coCartesian lift.

proof.text: By the fiber hypothesis, in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the coherent cocone category $P_{h'}$ of $h':J\to E_s$ in the quasicategory $E_s$ has an initial object $\iota$. Let $J_{h'}$ be the join slice of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] for $a=h'$, $L=J$ and $\mathcal E=E_s$: its vertices are exactly the simplicial maps $J^{\triangleright}\to E_s$ restricting to $h'$ on $J$. By that node the comparison $J_{h'}\to P_{h'}$, sending such a map to its induced coherent cocone, is a functor equivalence; choose a quasi-inverse $G$ and an equivalence edge from the image of $c'=G(\iota)$ to $\iota$. Precomposition with an equivalence edge is a homotopy equivalence of mapping spaces, since its component class is invertible and composition is associative and unital up to homotopy [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]; hence the coherent cocone of $c'$ is again initial, i.e. colimiting. By the last clause of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] $c'$ is also initial in $J_{h'}$. Thus $c':J^{\triangleright}\to E_s$ is a colimit cocone with $c'|_J=h'$ exactly. Regard $c'$ as a diagram in $E$ by the fiber inclusion. This choice is available also for $J=\varnothing$, when $c'$ is an initial object of $E_s$; no filteredness or contractibility of $J$ is used.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.1.11 proof, p. 267: assumption (1) and the choice of a colimit $\bar q'_0:K^{\triangleright}\to X_s$ of $q'_0$ in the fiber; the strict join form of the chosen cocone uses the join-slice/coherent-cocone comparison (HTT Proposition 4.2.1.5).

proof.text: For every edge $f:s\to s'$ of $B$, the transported cocone $f_!c'$ is colimiting in $E_{s'}$, because $f_!$ preserves $J$-indexed colimits by hypothesis: the coherent cocone induced by $f_!c'$ is $f_!$ applied to the coherent cocone of $c'$, since precomposition with $J\times\Delta^1\to J^{\triangleright}$ commutes with postcomposition by $f_!$. Hence [lem-coef-infinity-fiber-relative-colimit-criterion], applied to $c'$ and $p$, says that the inclusion of $c'$ into $E$ is a $p$-colimit diagram. In particular the cone vertex of $c'$ is a valid relative colimit apex for the transported diagram.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.1.11 proof, p. 267, using Proposition 4.3.1.10 after choosing $q'_0$.

proof.text: Put $T=J\times\Delta^1$, $A=J\times\{1\}$ and $D=T\amalg_A A^{\triangleright}$. Since $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is right anodyne, [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], with second monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow J$, makes $A\hookrightarrow T$ right anodyne (after interchanging product factors). Apply the pushout-join clause of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to this inclusion and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. Its domain is exactly $D$ and its target is $T^{\triangleright}$, so $D\hookrightarrow T^{\triangleright}$ is inner anodyne. The class of maps with the left lifting property against all inner fibrations, the lifting-class meaning of inner anodyne in [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], contains the inner horn inclusions and is closed under pushouts, transfinite composites and retracts, so it contains every inner anodyne map in the saturated sense of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]; and $p$ is an inner fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. On $D$ glue $Q_0$ and $c'$ along their common restriction $h'$ on $A$. Let $a:T\to J^{\triangleright}$ be the contraction used in Step 1. Extend $a$ to $\rho:T^{\triangleright}\to J^{\triangleright}$ by sending the new cone vertex to the old cone vertex: explicitly take $a^{\triangleright}:T^{\triangleright}\to(J^{\triangleright})^{\triangleright}=J\star\Delta^1$ and then the join map induced by $\Delta^1\to\Delta^0$. The restriction of $g\rho$ to $A^{\triangleright}$ is constant at $s$, so the glued map lies over $g\rho|_D$. Lifting gives $r:T^{\triangleright}\to E$ over $g\rho$ extending both pieces. Define $\kappa:J^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1\to T^{\triangleright}$ to be the identity on $J\times\Delta^1$ and to collapse $\{*\}\times\Delta^1$ to the new cone vertex. On an $n$-simplex its initial block of $J$-vertices is sent to the corresponding simplex of $J\times\Delta^1$ and its remaining cone-vertex block to the new cone vertex; this commutes with every face and degeneracy. Put $Q=r\kappa$ and $v=Q|_{J^{\triangleright}\times\{0\}}$. Then $Q|_{J^{\triangleright}\times\{1\}}=c'$, $Q|_{J\times\Delta^1}=Q_0$, and $Q|_{\{*\}\times\Delta^1}$ is the degenerate edge at $x=c'(*)$. Moreover $\rho\kappa$ is the identity at time $0$ and constant at the cone vertex at time $1$, so $v|_J=h$ and $pv=g$ exactly. When $J=\varnothing$, $D\to T^{\triangleright}$ is the identity of $\Delta^0$ and $v=c'$; no endpoint horn lift is required.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.1.11, printed p. 267: the intermediate cone (K times Delta^1)^right and its lift r. The text calls the left inclusion an inner fibration; the required property is inner anodyne, justified by the cited pushout-product and pushout-join statements (Kerodon 4.2.5.3 and 4.3.6.4).

proof.text: Write $\lambda:h\to h'$ for $Q_0$, $\eta:g|_J\to\Delta_Js$ for its base, and $x=c'(*)=v(*)$. Fix any vertex $z$ of $E$. Set $M_1=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,E)}(h',\Delta_Jz)$, $M_0=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,E)}(h,\Delta_Jz)$, $N_1=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,B)}(\Delta_Js,\Delta_J(pz))$ and $N_0=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,B)}(g|_J,\Delta_J(pz))$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], $p_J:\operatorname{Fun}(J,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,B)$ is a cocartesian fibration and $\lambda$ is $p_J$-cocartesian. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $p_J$, $\lambda$ and the target $\Delta_Jz$. It gives the homotopy-pullback square with upper row $M_1\xrightarrow{\lambda^*}M_0$, lower row $N_1\xrightarrow{\eta^*}N_0$, and vertical maps induced by $p$. Unlike the fiber formula for a target lying over $\Delta_Js$, this full mapping-square criterion allows the arbitrary target $\Delta_Jz$ lying over $\Delta_J(pz)$. Let $\alpha_1:h'\to\Delta_Jx$ be the coherent cocone of $c'$. Since $c'$ is a $p$-colimit by Step 3, [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] gives the homotopy-pullback square with upper row $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\xrightarrow{u\mapsto\Delta_J(u)\alpha_1}M_1$ and lower row $\operatorname{Map}_B(s,pz)\to N_1$. Both assertions apply to every $z$, with no requirement that $pz=s$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.9, printed pp. 264-265: expanded mapping-space proof for a degenerate apex component; uses the existing constant-target criterion (Kerodon Proposition 7.1.6.19, colimit dual).

proof.text: The two squares of Step 5 are adjacent in the diagram with upper row $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\to M_1\to M_0$ and lower row $\operatorname{Map}_B(s,pz)\to N_1\to N_0$. By [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], their outer rectangle is a homotopy pullback. Identify its maps and its commutation homotopy as follows. Precompose $Q$ with the product of the contraction $a:J\times\Delta^1\to J^{\triangleright}$ and the identity of the time interval. This gives a map $J\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to E$, hence a coherent square whose four edges are the cocone $\alpha_0:h\to\Delta_Jx$ of $v$, the cocone $\alpha_1$ of $c'$, $\lambda$, and the degenerate edge of $\Delta_Jx$. The two triangles with vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)$ and $(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)$ share the diagonal. Their composition witnesses, with the unit homotopy for the degenerate edge, give $\alpha_0\simeq\alpha_1\lambda$. The composition and unit homotopies are those of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]; these triangles are present as coherent diagrams, not just equalities of component classes. Applying the simplicial map $p$ gives the identical construction for $p\alpha_0\simeq(p\alpha_1)\eta$. Postcomposition with $u:x\to z$ consequently identifies the upper composite of the outer rectangle with $u\mapsto\Delta_J(u)\alpha_0$, and the lower composite with the corresponding map defined by $p\alpha_0$. The triangles retain all $J$-parameters, and their images under $p$ are precisely the base triangles, so this is the specified homotopy-commuting square, including its path coordinate, for the constant-target test of $v$. The homotopy-commuting clause of [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] therefore applies. Since it is a homotopy pullback for every $z$, [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] says that $v$ is a $p$-colimit diagram in the definition of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Step 4 already gives $v|_J=h$ and $pv=g$ exactly. For empty $J$, Step 4 gives $v=c'$ directly; for nonempty $J$ the same squares and triangles apply without any contractibility assumption.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.9 and the conclusion of Corollary 4.3.1.11, printed pp. 264-267; mapping-square argument expanded using Kerodon Proposition 7.1.6.19 and homotopy-pullback pasting (Proposition 3.4.1.11).
